title: MZ RPG Maker MZ crashing when I try to do ANYTHING

posts.author: Linthal
posts.body:
So as soon as I start the program, after the splash screen, I get to the main engine screen, but the moment I click on ANYTHING, the program closes. No error, no nothing. I am running Windows 11, I verified the windows integrity with an sfc scan. I have updated my graphics drivers, and disabled antivirus. I am running on multiple monitors.
In event viewer, its saying its having an error with d3d11.dll
does anyone have any ideas, or suggestions? This is very frustrating.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
I recommend checking the software's file integrity and not necessarily Window's integrity.
Though to be honest, it rarely solves the problem, it's always a good starting point. Uninstalling and reinstalling would also effectively do the same, but still doesn't hurt to run the integrity check just in case. You can do it from Steam by right clicking the software in your library -> properties -> Installed Files -> Verify Integrity of Software Files
It would also help if you posted your system specs, just so we can make sure you are meeting the hardware requirements.
I'm on my Linux machine atm, so I don't recall exactly off the top of my head, but I do think it's as simple as right clicking the windows button -> system information.
the d3d11.dll has me wondering if you changed graphics card recently at some point? It's a bit of a shot in the dark, so we won't go down troubleshooting that route until we checked other possible sources of the problem.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
Linthal said:
I have updated my graphics drivers,
Click to expand...
How did you do that?
Windows driver update is NOT reliable, the only way to correctly install the graphics driver is to download the setup from the manufacturer's website (either nVidia, AMD or Intel - there are no others left to my knowledge) and run that setup.
DON'T use the Microsoft-Programmed drivers that are favored by the internal automatic driver update, those are programmed for multiple chips and for general stability, only the manufacturer focuses on the optimal driver for each different graphic card.

posts.author: Deleted member 223646
posts.body:
Of course, check GPU drivers are correct and up to date.
Other ideas to try:
This could be a nw.js version issue. RPGMaker ships with an old version and is basically a nw.js/chromium app running through direct3d. (D3D11)
So instead of the WebGL rendering over D3D11 we can try force OpenGL to test.
If your RPG Maker MZ is the Steam version, try this:
In Steam -> right click
RPG Maker MZ
-> Properties -> Launch Options, and add:
--disable-gpu
Test and see if it is stable. If yes,  you may need to manually update the nw.js runtime in your RPGMaker install.
Other thoughts:
- overlays can sometimes cause this behaviour (nvidia experince, discord, etc)

posts.author: Deleted member 223646
posts.body:
So... you've actually possibly got three GPUs going there?
Does your processor have Intel UHD 630 iGPU
?
Have you got drivers in place for that one?
(I'd assume likely yes, but always gotta ask
)
regarding the two physical GPUs installed:
A test to try, if you're confident doing so:
Open Device Manager, go to Display adapters.
Make sure your monitors are in the 2060S.
Right-click the GTX 970, Disable device
(don’t uninstall)
.
Launch RPGM.
No crash - might be a driver conflict at play.
If crashing, re-enable 970, apply, plug screens into that one, and disable the 2060S next.
(Again, don't uninstall)
Launch RPGM.
No crash, as above, possible a driver conflict.
If crashing still, our issue is elsewhere.
If it is a driver conflict, we can instruct RPGM to specifically run on a desired GPU and 'not pick for itself' - but let's get tests outta the way.
Other ideas:
I see 'App Control for Business policy is enabled in your log also, even if the user mode is off, this might be a culprit - a quick test is boot into safe mode with networking and see if RPGM will run without a crash in that mode - if stable, this might be an indicator and we can look further into that.
Additionally, some more steam launch options to try, as
--disable-gpu
didn't yield a useful result:
1:
--use-angle=gl --disable-direct-composition
2:
--use-angle=d3d9 --disable-direct-composition
3:
--disable-gpu-compositing
4:
--disable-zero-copy
5:
--disable-features=UseSkiaRenderer
